lines.text: A small sultanate on the coast of Borneo that once ruled much of the island, and grew rich on oil. This is the story of Brunei.
From the fourteenth century Brunei was a Muslim sultanate. At its height, in the fifteen hundreds, it ruled the coasts of Borneo and parts of the Philippines.
In 1914 Omar Ali Saifuddien was born. As sultan, he would become the architect of modern Brunei.
By then Brunei was a British protectorate. In 1929 oil was struck at Seria, and the little state's fortunes changed for good.
In 1946 his son Hassanal Bolkiah was born. Sultan since 1967, he is one of the longest-reigning monarchs in the world.
In the fifties a mosque with a golden dome rose over the capital, named after the sultan who built it.
In December 1962 a revolt broke out against the sultan, and British troops put it down.
In 1974 the country founded its own national airline, Royal Brunei.
And in 1984 Brunei became fully independent from Britain.
That same year the sultan's new palace was finished, Istana Nurul Iman, the largest residential palace in the world.
Small, wealthy and ruled by one long reign, Brunei remains a sultanate like no other.
